annotations.title: Check a simulation model for errors before running it

description: Checks a model for mistakes before you run it and lists every problem it finds. It looks for loops with no delay, nodes that are not connected, unknown distributions, missing or invalid distribution parameters, and broken formulas. A loop, including an edge from a node to itself, is allowed and is not an error when at least one edge in it has delay 1 or more. Use this when you have built or edited a model and want to fix it without spending a run. To see what a run will cost, use estimate_simulation_size_and_cost instead. It returns is_valid and a list of issues. Each issue gives the rule broken, a severity (error, warning or info, where info is only a note), a message, and the node and edge ids involved. If an edge points at a node that does not exist, you get an error message instead of the list. Cost: free, with or without an account -- it debits no credits and spends none of your free daily runs. Without an account, a model over 1,000 trials or 20 nodes is rejected, also at no cost.

graph.description: The model: root_nodes (uncertain inputs), calc_nodes (formulas), edges (links; formulas refer to them like {e1}) and run_params (trials and time periods). Same format as run_monte_carlo_simulation's graph, which documents formulas, periods, distributions and financial metrics in full. Only this outline is published here: the full schema is on run_monte_carlo_simulation's graph parameter, and the neumann://catalog resource lists every distribution and formula function. Neumann checks the model against that full schema when you call this tool and names any problem.
